_comment: Maps LeRobot so101_follower joint values recorded with use_degrees=True to this repository's URDF.
LeRobot's 0 deg is the middle of each joint's calibrated range; the URDF's 0 rad is the arm pointing straight up.
For each arm joint: urdf_deg = sign * lerobot_deg + offset_deg (sign is +1 or -1).
offset_deg is the URDF angle of the pose where LeRobot reports 0 deg; sign is -1 when the joint turns the opposite way.
NOMINAL values, not a measurement of a specific arm. They come from TheRobotStudio's
Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf, whose zero pose is LeRobot's calibrated mid-range: there the upper arm
leans 14.0 deg forward of vertical, the forearm points 87.9 deg from vertical and the wrist 90.0 deg, giving
pitch offsets 14.0, 73.9 and 2.1 deg in this URDF's straight-up convention. shoulder_pan (-Z vs +Z) and
wrist_roll (axis reversed) turn the opposite way. wrist_roll's zero cannot be derived because this URDF
models the gripper as a sliding jaw, so its offset is assumed 0.
Verify on your arm (pose it at known URDF angles and read LeRobot's degrees). Mapped values outside this
URDF's joint limits are rejected by normalize_so101_dataset.py. Those limits (joint_limits.json) are
so101_new_calib.urdf's limits mapped with these nominal values; re-derive them if you change them.
gripper.closed/open are LeRobot's 0-100 gripper readings at fully closed and at 0.04 m opening.
LeRobot's default use_degrees=False (-100..100) data cannot be mapped without the arm's calibration file and is rejected.
